method: Read all 50 unique English-source groups for every file. Verified the remaining repeated occurrences by equality within English-source groups, then ran the exported validator and exact UTF-8/4-space/final-newline format check. Semantic review covered unknown domain/IP registration, origin server, wait limits, excess requests, unusual connections, optional JavaScript and expected maintenance return.

files.notes: Bosnian Latin standard is consistent (izvinjavamo, zahtjev, server). Source distinctions and modal strength are preserved.
Bosnian Cyrillic retains Ijekavian forms and the same meaning as the Latin standard; technical identifiers remain Latin as required. No accidental Serbian Ekavian substitution identified.
Croatian choices are coherent (poslužitelj, pogreška, trenutačno, web-mjesto). Origin server and excessive-request explanations are explicit.
Slovenian semantics are coherent. Refined insecure-request title to unsecured, avoiding an unnecessary implication that the request is dangerous.
Estonian preserves origin server, timed-out wait, domain/IP association and expected maintenance recovery. No concrete correction identified.
Latvian grammar and technical register preserve the source meaning. No concrete correction identified.
Icelandic web terminology and cases are coherent. Timeout and conditional maintenance recovery remain distinct. No concrete correction identified.
Faroese is recognizably distinct from Icelandic/Danish. Meaning is preserved; technical compounds, case government and idiomatic phrasing remain lower review confidence.
Nynorsk forms are consistent (ikkje, førespurnad, tenar, mellombels). No Bokmål substitution or substantive meaning issue identified.
Luxembourgish text is coherent and distinct from German. Technical register and local orthographic preferences have lower review confidence; no certain error identified.
West Frisian text is coherent and distinct from Dutch. Technical compounds and local idiom merit further fluent review; no certain source-meaning defect identified.

Irish source semantics are preserved, including expired time, excessive requests and expected recovery. Initial mutations and specialized phrasing merit additional fluent review; no definite correction identified.

fixes.reason: In the HTTPS/protocol context, unsecured is more precise than a term also read as dangerous. Keeps the source claim about security, without adding an assertion of maliciousness.

limitations: Independent model review is not native-speaker certification. No unresolved certain semantic defect remains; lower-confidence languages may benefit from local terminology/idiom refinement.
